title: High bandstands in the old halls
summary: Discussion of halls with raised bandstands, Nunciation Street club, Artesian, Economy, Perseverance and Francs Amis halls.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh, just the bandstand was up high.

Yeah, the bandstand was up high. People used to dance down. The cabaret was on the first floor. The cabaret was on the first floor. The bandstand was up looking down on the floor. Yeah. They got that carnival, that club uptown got the bandstand like that. Cause I played up there a couple of years ago. Up there, the club up there on, you know, Irish Channel, big club, carnival club. They got a bandstand upstairs. They got a beautiful club up there.
What street is that on?
That's on, that's on, uh, Nunciation I think. Nunciation Street.
Nunciation.
Mm-hmm. We lived there one time.
I don't remember that club. There was one hall there where the Buzzards have, they used to have dances where Joe Avery used to play.
Yeah, he did too.

But the bandstand wasn't up high. I don't know that club you're talking about then. On the Nunciation you think? I'd like to take a picture of it sometime. There's another club on Magazine Street I think is still there.
Magazine Street too, yeah. They got a lot of different clubs up there but that's where I used to play it. I played once or twice different dances, you know.
Was it up above Jackson on Nunciation Street then?
Yeah, it's up above there.
Yeah, probably there. It was a big hall I remember.

Yeah, it's a big hall with a big bandstand up there cause I know we had to cram up the stairs to go up there, you know. Most of the halls that they were in the hall, the hall that they built in was the bandstand was way up. It would be better for you, you know what I mean? Cause right on the floor you'd be in the way of the people and you'd be up there out the way, you see. Music would sound better. It's a mile out there, you know. Because that's the way the old time halls used to have the bandstand up. If I was to have a hall that's where I'd put my bandstand upstairs and let them look down on the public.
Did it get sorta hot up there sometime though?
Well no, it wasn't hot up there. Yeah, sometime it got hot at the carburetors cause you're so close to the ceiling.
Yeah, that's what that was. And over here at Artesian Hall too.

Well, Artesian Hall too, that bandstand railing, well they did have a bigger, right here they had a bigger, you know, place for the band up there, a bigger gallery. But right here they had like a little gallery, wide as my gallery out there. I've never been in the Perseverance Hall. What does it look like inside the Perseverance?
Is that old balcony still there for the bandstand? Did they tear that out?
No, I believe they threw that out. I never been in there. I never knew the sense I've been in. I went in there one day in the church. I never knew it.

The Economy Hall still has the big bandstand. We took some pictures of that. Yeah. Like in the old days, it's still there. And of course Artesian Hall is the same. I believe they got it up there yet. I wondered about Perseverance if it's up there.
I believe it's up there yet, but they made the altar there. You know, they blocked it off, I believe. It's nothing there now, but the altar's there.
What was Franz and Me Hall like in the old days? Was the, did they have a high bandstand up high?

Franz and Me Hall? Yeah, they had a whole upstate. The whole bandstand up there. The bandstand up there. Most all the halls had it. The New Hall, the phones I mean. The New Hall was too. Yeah, bandstand up there.
I think New Hall is all torn out now. I remember there one day they were having some games in there.
Yeah, they had a keynote game. Keno or something. Yeah.
